response.overview: *www.gilgamesh.21 (2007)* *A film by Tariq Hashim*  Through online conversations and webcams, Tariq and Basim exchange conversations about loneliness, alienation, fear, and longing for home, in a dialogue that reveals the paradox of life between one who lives the cold hell of exile, and one who faces the hell of war in Baghdad. Between the desire to return and the desire to survive, the film evokes the legend of Gilgamesh in a contemporary reading of the meaning of homeland, exile, and loss.  In this cold space lit by screen flashes and intersecting images, another element slips into the frame to carry the weight of the entire scene; it is the dog. The dog does not appear in the film as a pet or a passing decorative element, but was carefully employed to be a living mirror for characters living their alienation in silence, as if the director wanted through this character to give silence a voice. The dog does not speak, just as the human characters sometimes fail
